claims: Wallet login is officially supported
WalletConnect is supported
Connecting on BNB Chain requires at least 0.001 BNB
Email login is officially supported
A new blockchain address is created for the email address
Email-login deposits are currently limited to USDT on Arbitrum
After deposit, the email-created address can be used as collateral on Aster Pro
Aster Pro API allows users to operate securely using API keys
Users should first create an API key, then use API documentation
Users go to API management and connect wallet
Users click Create API and receive API key plus secret key
Each account can create up to 30 API keys
IP binding is recommended
API management page is live
Each account can create up to 30 API keys
Some endpoints require an API key
API keys are passed via X-MBX-APIKEY header
SIGNED endpoints use HMAC SHA256
API keys can be permission-scoped
Builder address must be registered and have at least 100 ASTER
Builder backend generates a per-user Agent/API Wallet signer
Users approve Agent and Builder separately or together
Builder places orders on behalf of the user through fapi/v3 endpoints

conclusion: Aster currently exposes a standard self-serve Pro API key path for direct traders, and that should not be conflated with the separate Aster Code builder/agent delegation stack. The direct API path is materially simpler than the first-pass builder-only framing, while the delegated builder flow remains a distinct higher-friction integration mode.
